Intelligence Brief / N° 127 · HOT · F1

Fluidstack

AI Infrastructure · GPU Cloud / Data-Centre Builder · New York (founded in Oxford, 2017) · Private (~$18B reported; $1.5B round, Sep 2026)

Fluidstack, the Oxford-born AI-infrastructure builder now constructing Anthropic's $50B US data-centre programme, has reportedly closed a $1.5B round led by Jane Street at an $18B valuation (Forbes, 3 Sep 2026), more than doubling the $7.5B mark it set only in July.

76
Opportunity / 100
Timing window
HOT
Series
F1
Recommended team
Atlassian Williams Racing
Action horizon
6-10 WKS

The case

Forbes reported on 3 September that Fluidstack raised $1.5B led by Jane Street at an $18B valuation; Crunchbase News puts total funding just over $2.6B. The company has not announced the round. It closed a ~$750M round at ~$7.5B in July after Bloomberg-sourced talks in April, so the price has more than doubled in two months. The business behind it is real: Anthropic's $50B US infrastructure programme, announced 12 Nov 2025, starts with Fluidstack-built data centres in Texas and New York, with sites coming online through 2026.

The grid has already priced this archetype: CoreWeave became Aston Martin Aramco's Official AI Cloud Computing Partner in May 2025, and Core Scientific sits on Cadillac's first roster. Jane Street is the common thread, having committed billions of compute spend to CoreWeave and Crusoe before backing Fluidstack outright. Fluidstack is the one of the three with no seat, and its anchor customer's brand, Claude, already races on a Williams.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Forbes reported on 3 September that Fluidstack has raised $1.5B led by Jane Street at an $18B valuation; Crunchbase News puts total funding at just over $2.6B. The company has not announced the round itself, so this is reported, not confirmed, and the brief says so.
Price doubled in two months
In April Bloomberg reported Jane Street in talks at an $18B target; Fluidstack instead closed a ~$750M round at ~$7.5B in July. Two months later the $18B print landed. A company re-priced that fast has a story to tell to enterprise buyers, bankers and the public markets, and a budget to tell it with.
The Anthropic build-out
Anthropic's $50B US infrastructure programme, announced 12 November 2025, starts with Fluidstack-built data centres in Texas and New York, with sites coming online through 2026. Each site that goes live is a milestone the partnership can be timed to.
Calendar window
The United States GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026; teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and activated in full for 2027.

Why Atlassian Williams Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Williams carries Atlassian as title partner, VAST Data for the data platform, Keeper for identity security, Airia and Brillio on the technology side, and Claude as Official Thinking Partner. No cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner: Official AI Compute Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The warm path
Fluidstack builds Anthropic's data centres; Anthropic's Claude has been on the Williams car since the February livery reveal, working with the team's engineers and strategists. The introduction can run through a partner Williams already trusts, and the activation can pair the model with the compute beneath it.
A team that will use the product
Williams' revival is data-led. Elastic GPU capacity for surrogate models, simulation and analytics is consumed in the factory, not just displayed on the car, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.
Story and market fit
Oxford-founded, now New York-headquartered: a British origin story for a British team and a US identity for the Austin and Las Vegas rounds where Fluidstack's customers and investors sit.

Audi F1 TeamHewlett Packard Enterprise on the roster in the last 12 months; lane crowded.
TGR Haas F1 Team · Racing BullsOpen but not chosen: neither carries the Anthropic tie that gives Williams a warm path.

Value To Atlassian Williams Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Compute for the work outside the aerodynamic-testing restrictions: machine-learning surrogates, driver-in-the-loop and race-strategy simulation, telemetry and video analytics between sessions. Fluidstack supplies it on demand; the team gets capacity it could not fund inside the cost cap.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner that sells to CIOs, CFOs and hyperscalers brings a guest list of enterprise buyers, investors and bankers to Austin and Las Vegas, the audience Williams' B2B partners want in the suite.
Content and ecosystem
The model and the compute on one car: co-produced engineering content with the Claude programme, a factory reference customer for Fluidstack's enterprise sales, and a data-centre-to-pit-wall story the team can tell on camera.
What the team gives back
Official AI Compute Partner designation, engine-cover or sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, driver and engineering access for Fluidstack's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Compute Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the Anthropic build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $4-7M a year, part-payable in compute credits. Scope: engine-cover or sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, US-race hospitality, engineering content with the Claude programme.

The askA 25-minute call with Gary Wu before the United States GP to confirm the round on the record, agree an Austin announcement window, and size an Official AI Compute Partner entry against Williams' 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Gary Wu
Co-Founder & CEO, Fluidstack · verified
Wu co-founded Fluidstack in Oxford in 2017 and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: César Maklary, Co-Founder and President (commercial), and Rob Perdue, COO since February 2025. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the Claude connection.
“Gary, Claude already races on the Williams; you build Anthropic's compute. CoreWeave took its seat at Aston Martin in the year of its listing, and the compute lane at Williams is open. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A reported $1.5B round at $18B, a $50B Anthropic build-out on Fluidstack sites, and Claude already on the Williams put Fluidstack at peak brand-investment authority with a warm path in. The compute lane at Williams is open and two US races remain inside the window.

Crusoe

AI Infrastructure · GPU Cloud / Datacentre Builder · Denver, Colorado · Private (~$30B reported; $3B+ Series F, Sep 2026)

Crusoe, the energy-first AI-infrastructure builder behind OpenAI's 1.2 GW Abilene campus, has reportedly closed a $3B+ Series F at a ~$30B valuation (Bloomberg, 3 Sep 2026), nearly tripling its October 2025 mark, days after a reported ~$13B five-year Jane Street cloud contract.

The case

Crusoe's reported $3B+ Series F at roughly $30B post-money, co-led by Atreides Management and Valor Equity Partners with Mubadala Capital participating, nearly triples the $10B+ valuation set by its $1.375B Series E in October 2025. The company builds and powers gigawatt-scale AI data centres - the first phase of the 1.2 GW Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas is live for Oracle and OpenAI - and sells GPU cloud to OpenAI, Microsoft and Meta. Bloomberg also reports a ~$13B, five-year AI-cloud contract with Jane Street, its highest-profile cloud customer yet.

The grid has already proved this archetype buys F1: CoreWeave signed with Aston Martin Aramco in May 2025 as Official AI Cloud Computing Partner, and Core Scientific joined Cadillac for 2026. Crusoe's closest rival is on the grid and Crusoe is not, and no team carries a brand that owns both halves of the AI build-out, the power and the compute.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Bloomberg reported on 3 September that Crusoe closed more than $3B of Series F capital at roughly $30B post-money, co-led by Atreides Management and Valor Equity Partners with Mubadala Capital participating. That is close to three times the valuation set by its $1.375B Series E in October 2025, and it lands in the same week as a reported ~$13B, five-year AI-cloud contract with Jane Street.
Budget authority
A raise of this size resets the brand and marketing budget for the next 12 to 18 months. With OpenAI, Microsoft, Meta and now Jane Street already on the customer list, the next buyers Crusoe has to reach are enterprise CIOs, CFOs and the capital-markets audience ahead of a probable listing. That is the audience a Formula 1 partnership puts in the room.
Calendar window
The US GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two remaining home-market races of 2026. A partnership agreed before Austin can be announced there and activated in full for 2027; teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter.
Competitive clock
CoreWeave, Crusoe's closest listed rival, has held the Official AI Cloud Computing Partner slot at Aston Martin Aramco since May 2025, and Core Scientific joined Cadillac for 2026. Fluidstack raised a reported $1.5B at an $18B valuation this week and is the next name likely to shop for a grid position. The open cloud-compute lanes will not stay open through 2027.

The open lane
Haas carries no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner. Its technology roster is Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner, Mphasis for digital services and RUCKUS Networks for networking, which leaves Official AI Cloud Compute Partner a clean, ownable category at a team-partner price rather than a title price.
Audience and market fit
Haas is the American privateer in a US-owned sport; Crusoe is a Denver company whose growth story (Abilene, Wyoming, Jane Street) is American. Austin and Las Vegas are US rounds still to come in 2026, and the team's guest lists at those events are the enterprise and capital-markets buyers Crusoe is selling to.
A team that will use the product
Haas is the grid's lean privateer, so it has the most to gain from elastic GPU capacity for simulation, strategy and analytics work. The partnership would be consumed in the factory, not just displayed on the car, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.
Precedent and price
CoreWeave's Aston Martin deal proves a neocloud buys Formula 1. The Haas lane comes at a team-partner entry tier, an estimated $5-8M a year and part-payable in compute credits, with sidepod placement and naming of the team's compute environment. The precedent removes the category doubt; the price makes it an easy first commitment.

Octopus Energy Group

Energy Retail & Technology · Renewable Supply, EV Charging, Grid Flexibility · London · Private ($9B, May 2024)

Octopus Energy, Britain's largest household supplier with £13.7bn of revenue and 10 million customers, closed its majority investment in US grid-flexibility company Uplight on 1 September, eight months after selling a $1B stake in Kraken at $8.65B. The most EV-native energy brand has never been on an electric racing car.

The case

On 1 September Octopus Energy Group completed its majority investment in Uplight, which manages 8.5 GW of flexible load for more than 85 US utilities; Schneider Electric stays as minority partner and Nick Chaset runs Uplight alongside Octopus Energy US. It caps a year of capital re-shaping: $850M of the $1B Kraken stake sale (December 2025, $8.65B valuation) went to Octopus, on top of a $9B valuation set by Generation Investment Management and CPP Investments in May 2024. The year to 30 April 2025 brought £13.7bn of revenue, up 10%, and 10 million customers.

The brand is built on electric cars. Electroverse reaches more than 1 million public chargers in over 40 countries, Ford integrated it into its own charging network in September 2025, and more than half of Britain's 653,000 smart EV-tariff customers are with Octopus. It already knows long-term sport: Arsenal's official energy partner since October 2016. What it lacks is a stage where the product is the sport itself.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Octopus Energy Group completed its majority investment in Uplight on 1 September 2026. Uplight stays an independent company, Schneider Electric remains a minority partner, and Nick Chaset becomes Uplight's CEO alongside his role running Octopus Energy US. The stated targets are $1 billion of customer savings and more than doubling flexible capacity to 20 GW over five years.
A year of capital re-shaping
In December 2025 Octopus sold a $1B stake in Kraken at an $8.65B valuation, with $850M of the proceeds going to the group, and set a mid-2026 target for full separation. The group itself was valued at $9B in May 2024 when Generation Investment Management and CPP Investments increased their stakes. A company that has just re-cut its own identity needs a new way to explain itself to customers and investors.
The numbers underneath
In the year to 30 April 2025 Octopus recorded £13.7bn of revenue, up 10%, and grew to 10 million customers, including 7.6m UK homes. It reported a £255m net loss after one-off items, which is why the brief sizes the entry at partner level and includes an in-kind supply component.
Calendar window
Formula E's Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18 December 2026 and reaches London on 29-30 May 2027. A partnership agreed in the fourth quarter is announced at the season launch and activated in full at the home race.

Why Jaguar Tcs Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Jaguar TCS Racing carries TCS as title and technology partner, Castrol and the Jaguar powertrain. There is no energy retailer, EV-charging or home-energy brand on the roster, so Official Energy Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
Jaguar's relaunch
The road brand is relaunching electric-only in 2026 with its first new car sold from Bond Street, the first of three new electric Jaguars. Every buyer needs a home tariff and a public charging network; Octopus sells both, and Ford has already shown that an OEM will integrate Electroverse into its own charging offer.
Two British electrification stories
Britain's largest household supplier and Britain's electric racing team, with a home race in London. The partnership reads as a national story rather than a badge.
A team that uses its partners
The TCS partnership runs across the team's operations rather than sitting on the car. Octopus's supply, charging and flexibility products fit the same pattern.

An Intelligent Octopus Go plus Electroverse bundle offered to buyers of the new electric Jaguars in the UK, on the model Ford adopted in September 2025, giving the team's parent a customer proposition and Octopus a premium acquisition channel.

A consumer brand with 10 million customers brings a mass audience to the London E-Prix and a hospitality guest list of fleet, utility and government buyers. The Arsenal partnership shows Octopus activates for a decade, not a season.

A $9B energy brand whose product is electric driving, fresh from the Uplight close and the Kraken proceeds, with a proven ten-year sports partnership and no presence in electric racing. Jaguar TCS Racing's energy lane is open and the London E-Prix is its home stage.

Fervo Energy

Clean Firm Power · Enhanced Geothermal · Houston, Texas · Nasdaq: FRVO (IPO 13 May 2026 at $27)

Fervo Energy, the Houston enhanced-geothermal developer that listed on Nasdaq in May in clean energy's largest-ever IPO, signed a 396 MW, 15-year power purchase agreement with Google on 1 September, the biggest enhanced-geothermal deal yet, weeks before its first Cape Station power flows in Utah.

Opportunity / 100
Timing window
HOT
Series
FE
Recommended team

Action horizon
8-14 WKS

The case

Fervo sold 70,000,000 shares at $27 on 13 May 2026, above the marketed range; with the greenshoe the 10-Q puts the raise at 80,500,000 shares and roughly $2.2B gross, and Fortune reported the stock opened about 35% higher, above a $10B value. It is still pre-revenue: Q2 revenue was $113,000 against a $55.9M net loss. What it has is power under contract: a 396 MW, 15-year PPA with Google Energy announced 1 September, expandable to nearly 1 GW by June 2030, and Cape Station Phase I in Utah targeting first power in Q4 2026 on the way to 1.1 GW by 2030.

Formula E is the electrification stage: ABB holds the championship title and Google Cloud, Fervo's anchor customer's sister brand, is a championship partner. On the grid the only power-generation name is Envision Group, which owns Envision Racing; the oil majors sit with DS Penske (TotalEnergies) and the Lola Yamaha ABT team (Shell). No team carries a clean firm-power brand, and the one American team, Andretti, has no energy partner at all.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 1 September Fervo announced a 396 MW, 15-year power purchase agreement with Google Energy for the Cape Station GeoCluster in Utah, signed on 26 August, with an option for Google to take nearly 1 GW by June 2030. It is the largest enhanced-geothermal contract yet, and it arrived less than four months after the company's Nasdaq listing.
From developer to producer
Cape Station Phase I (100 MW) is in commissioning: GeoBlock 1 first power is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026, with GeoBlocks 2 and 3 following in early 2027 and Phase II (400 MW) by 2028. A company that has spent nine years drilling becomes a power producer this quarter, which is the moment a brand story is worth paying for.
Budget authority
The IPO raised roughly $2.2B gross (80.5 million shares at $27, greenshoe included). Fervo is still pre-revenue, with Q2 revenue of $113,000 and a $55.9M net loss, so any sponsorship has to be sized as a marketing line, not a vanity line, and pointed at the audiences a newly public company must reach: utilities, hyperscalers, policymakers and public-market investors.
Calendar window
Season 13 opens with a Jeddah double-header on 18-19 December 2026 and Formula E races in Texas for the first time on 6 February 2027 at the Circuit of The Americas, with Miami a fortnight later. Teams close their GEN4 partner rosters in the fourth quarter; a deal agreed before Jeddah can be launched at COTA in front of a home-state audience.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E carries TWG AI as primary partner and Official Artificial Intelligence Partner, plus Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo. There is no energy, power or sustainability partner, so Official Clean Power Partner is an ownable category at a team-partner price on the one team where a Texas company has a home race.
A roster being redrawn
Porsche's powertrain supply ends after Season 12 and Andretti moves to Nissan powertrains for 2026-27 under the GEN4 regulations. A new technical partner, a new car and a fresh livery mean the team is deciding its partner line-up now, which is exactly when a first-time sponsor gets a fair hearing.
Audience and market fit
Andretti is the only American team in the championship, owned by TWG Global, and Formula E's US swing in February 2027 (Austin, then Miami) is the team's home ground. Fervo's buyers and investors are American utilities, hyperscalers and funds; COTA is a two-hour drive from Fervo's Houston headquarters.
Teams ruled out
Envision Racing is owned by Envision Group, a renewables and battery group that would not share the energy lane with a rival generator. DS Penske carries TotalEnergies and Lola Yamaha ABT carries Shell. Jaguar TCS, Nissan, Porsche, Mahindra, Cupra Kiro and Citroën are European or Asian works teams whose partner rosters and audiences give a Houston company no home stage.

Value To Andretti Formula E — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

What this is not (Mode B)
Fervo generates electricity for grids and data centres; it does not supply anything a race team consumes. There is no operational workstream, and the OPS FIT score of 10/20 reflects that honestly. The value is brand, audience and content, and each of those has a concrete mechanism below.
Brand and narrative for the team
Official Clean Power Partner gives Andretti a GEN4-era sustainability story that is about firm, round-the-clock power rather than offsets: the car races on electricity, the partner makes it. That is a narrative the team can carry on camera and into the championship's own sustainability programme without inventing anything.
Commercial lift for the team
A newly listed company brings a guest list the team's existing B2B partners want in the suite: utility executives, hyperscaler energy buyers (Google is Fervo's anchor customer and Google Cloud is a championship partner), infrastructure investors and bankers. Hospitality at Austin and Miami turns two US rounds into Fervo's investor and customer days.
Content and what the team gives back
Co-produced content pairing Fervo's drilling engineers with Andretti's race engineers: heat to electrons at Cape Station, braking to charge on a GEN4 car. In return the team provides rear-wing and sidepod placement, the partner designation, COTA and Miami hospitality, driver and engineering access for Fervo's customer and IR channels, and a Google co-activation.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Clean Power Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15 (2026/27-2028/29), spanning Cape Station Phase I and the 2028 Google GeoCluster. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a season at team-partner tier. Scope: rear-wing and sidepod placement, COTA and Miami hospitality, joint content, and a Google co-activation given Google Cloud's championship role.

Opening angle

Lead with the Texas debut.
“Tim, Formula E races in Texas for the first time on 6 February, your first Cape Station power flows this quarter, and the clean-power lane at the only American team is open. 25 minutes before Jeddah to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A May IPO of roughly $2.2B, a 396 MW Google contract signed in August and first Cape Station power due this quarter put Fervo at its brand-building peak as Formula E arrives in Texas. Andretti, the only American team, carries no energy partner and is redrawing its GEN4 livery now.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 141 · 05 SEP 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 141 · HOT · FE

Hydrostor

Long-Duration Energy Storage · Advanced Compressed-Air Storage Developer & Operator · Toronto (US HQ Denver, Colorado) · Private ($230M equity, Aug 2026; valuation not stated)

Hydrostor, the Toronto developer of cavern-scale compressed-air storage backed by Goldman Sachs, CPP Investments and Canada Growth Fund, closed a $230M equity investment on 12 August to carry its 500 MW Willow Rock plant in California to financial close this year and its Australian Silver City project into construction.

The case

On 12 August Hydrostor closed a $230M equity investment: the conversion of the note committed by Canada Growth Fund, Goldman Sachs Alternatives and CPP Investments in February 2025, plus a strategic round from Baker Hughes, Realize Capital Partners and Hatch. The new-money share is not broken out. It follows US$55M from Export Development Canada in September 2025 and Baker Hughes' January agreement pairing equity with up to 1.4 GW of equipment orders. The money has a stated job: a 7 GW pipeline and Willow Rock, 500 MW in Kern County, to financial close this year.

This is the half-year in which a developer becomes a builder. Willow Rock holds a California licence granted on 19 December 2025 and a 25-year offtake with Central Coast Community Energy worth about $1B; Silver City in Broken Hill won grid-connection approval on 2 September and is due to start construction. Goderich in Ontario has run commercially since 2020. A company about to pour concrete in two countries needs a public identity it lacks.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Hydrostor closed a $230M equity investment on 12 August 2026. It includes the conversion of the previously announced note from Canada Growth Fund, Goldman Sachs Alternatives and CPP Investments and a strategic equity round from returning investor Baker Hughes and new investors Realize Capital Partners and Hatch. The company does not break out the new-money portion, and the brief says so.
The capital stack behind it
February 2025 brought $200M from the same three institutions ($150M convertible note plus a $50M development loan). Export Development Canada added US$55M in September 2025 for Silver City. In January 2026 Baker Hughes, an investor since 2019, paired an equity investment with up to 1.4 GW of equipment orders. Capital of this quality is what makes a multi-year partnership bankable even without a stated valuation.
Developer to builder
Willow Rock in Kern County, California (500 MW) holds a state licence granted on 19 December 2025, a 25-year offtake with Central Coast Community Energy worth about $1B, and a further 50 MW offtake signed with California Community Power in February 2026; financial close is targeted later in 2026. Silver City in Broken Hill (200 MW) won grid-connection approval on 2 September 2026 and is due to start construction. The first plant, Goderich in Ontario, has operated commercially since 2020.
Calendar window
Formula E's Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18 December 2026; the Austin E-Prix follows on 6 February and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February 2027. A partnership agreed in the fourth quarter is announced at the season launch and activated in the United States within eight weeks.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E carries TWG AI as primary partner, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo, with Nissan powertrains from Season 13. There is no energy, storage, utility or grid brand on the roster, so Official Energy Storage Partner is a clean category at a partner price.
The American team for a US build-out
Hydrostor's US headquarters is in Denver and its flagship plant is in California. Andretti's Austin and Miami rounds land within weeks of Willow Rock's financial close, in front of the utilities, community-choice buyers and financiers Hydrostor sells to.
Why not the energy team
Envision Racing would be the natural fit, but its title partner Envision Group owns Envision AESC, a maker of grid-storage battery cells with a 60 GWh storage expansion under way. Hydrostor's compressed-air caverns compete with exactly that product.
Story fit
Formula E markets itself as the championship of electrification. Eight-hour storage that firms renewable power is the missing chapter in that story, and Andretti's content programme with TWG AI gives it a home.

Value To Andretti Formula E — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Halo, honestly stated (Mode B)
There is no operational workstream: cavern-scale storage has nothing to do on a race car, and the brief does not pretend otherwise. The value is commercial and narrative.
Audience the team wants
Utilities, community-choice aggregators, regulators and project-finance investors are a B2B audience Andretti's hospitality has not yet hosted. Hydrostor brings them to Austin and Miami, and the team's other partners get to meet them.
Content and ecosystem
Co-produced content on long-duration storage and grid reliability, a Willow Rock site activation with the team's US partners, and a technology narrative that complements TWG AI rather than competing with it.
What the team gives back
Official Energy Storage Partner designation, car and race-suit placement, Austin and Miami hospitality, driver access, and a platform for Hydrostor's first public brand campaign at the moment its plants become visible.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Energy Storage Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, spanning Willow Rock construction and the first Silver City operations. Estimated $1-2M a season at partner level. Scope: car and suit placement, Austin and Miami hospitality, co-produced content on long-duration storage, and a Willow Rock site activation.

The askA 25-minute call with Curtis VanWalleghem before the Jeddah opener on 18 December to confirm whether a brand budget exists alongside the project capital, and to size an Official Energy Storage Partner entry at Andretti Formula E for Seasons 13-15 timed to Willow Rock's financial close.

Primary decision-maker

Curtis VanWalleghem
Co-Founder & CEO, Hydrostor · verified
VanWalleghem launched Hydrostor in 2010 and fronts every raise, so a first brand partnership is his call. Path: Jon Norman, President; Jordan Cole, Chief Commercial Officer, ex-Brookfield; Beth Summers, Chief Financial Officer. No chief marketing officer is listed, which is itself the opening.

Opening angle

Lead with the construction moment.
“Curtis, Willow Rock closes and Silver City breaks ground in the same quarter Formula E launches Season 13; Andretti is the American team with an open energy lane and Austin and Miami in February. 25 minutes before Jeddah to see whether the timing works?”
Bottom line
A well-backed storage developer at the moment its first two utility-scale plants go to financial close and construction, with no brand, no CMO and no rival storage name on the Andretti roster. Partner-level, halo-honest, timed to the Season 13 launch and two US rounds in February.

Risks & counters

PROJECT MONEY, NOT BRAND MONEY
The $230M includes converted notes and is earmarked for a 7 GW pipeline; no valuation or marketing budget is stated and there is no CMO. Counter: Size at partner level, hospitality weighted to Austin and Miami; ask for the budget line on the first call.

Compressed-air caverns have nothing to do on a race car; the deal rests on story and audience. Counter: Anchor on Formula E's electrification message and a Willow Rock site activation; do not overclaim integration.

Base Power

Energy · Home Batteries & Grid Services · Austin, Texas (founded 2023) · Private ($13B post-money; $1B Series D, Aug 2026)

Base Power, the Austin company that installs grid-connected home batteries and sells the electricity behind them, closed a $1B Series D at a $13B post-money valuation on 3 August 2026, up from $4B last October, and launched Base Core, a 39.2 kWh battery built in its own Austin factory.

The case

Base Power announced on 3 August that it had raised a $1B Series D at a $13B post-money valuation, led by Ribbit, Addition, Valor Equity Partners and JPMorganChase's Strategic Investment Group, with Altimeter, Coatue and others alongside. It follows a $1B Series C led by Addition in October 2025 at $4B and a $200M Series B in April 2025; the company says it has raised more than $2.5B. The same release launched Base Core, a 39.2 kWh home battery in production at Base Factory 1 in Austin, with proceeds going to national expansion.

The model is the story: Base sells homeowners a cheap battery and cheap electricity, then dispatches thousands of batteries into the ERCOT market as a virtual power plant. Utilities now buy it wholesale, with CoServ signing for 100 MW across North Texas in March 2026, and Illinois opened on 24 June in ComEd territory. The all-electric championship arrives in Base's own city in February, with the money for a national launch already in the bank.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Base Power announced on 3 August 2026 a $1B Series D at a $13B post-money valuation, led by Ribbit, Addition, Valor Equity Partners and JPMorganChase's Strategic Investment Group. The company says it has raised more than $2.5B in total. This is company-announced, not press-reported: the release is on Business Wire and was covered the same day by TechCrunch.
Valuation tripled in ten months
The Series C of October 2025, $1B led by Addition, valued the company at $4B; the Series D puts it at $13B. A company re-priced that fast has a story to tell to homeowners, utilities and the public markets, and the release earmarks the money for taking Base Core to more homes and expanding nationally.
A product to launch
Base Core is a 39.2 kWh home battery designed and built at Base Factory 1 in Austin, available in Texas and Illinois. Sponsorship works hardest when there is a new product to put in front of people, and Base has one arriving state by state through the Season 13 calendar.
Calendar window
Formula E's GEN4 era opens with the Jeddah E-Prix on 18 December 2026. The Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027 is a race in Base's home city, and the Miami E-Prix follows on 20 February. Teams close their Season 13 partner rosters in the autumn, so a deal agreed in the next six to ten weeks can launch at the first US round.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E carries TWG AI as primary partner and Official AI Partner, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo, with Nissan supplying the GEN4 powertrain from Season 13. There is no energy, battery, storage or utility partner on the roster, and none at any other Formula E team: Official Energy Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The American team
Andretti is the American entry in an otherwise European and Asian grid, owned by TWG Motorsports. The Austin and Miami weekends are its home rounds as much as Base's, and an Austin company on an American car in Austin is the story local and national media will write.
A route to Formula 1
TWG Motorsports' parent, TWG Global, also fields the Cadillac F1 Team with General Motors. A Formula E entry that proves itself at the US rounds gives Base a relationship with the same owner when its footprint and budget justify Formula 1, without paying F1 prices for a two-state consumer brand today.
Audience fit
Formula E's partners are ABB, DHL, Julius Baer, Google Cloud and PIF: an electrification and sustainability audience. Base sells grid resilience to homeowners and dispatchable capacity to utilities such as CoServ, and its Head of Policy, Travis Kavulla, is a former state regulator; the series' hospitality is where those utility and policy conversations happen.

Base Core units powering the team's hospitality and fan zone at the Austin and Miami weekends, as a live demonstration of the product rather than a logo: the same battery that backs up a Texas home backing up the garage's guests.

A partner that sells to utilities, home builders and regulators brings a guest list of co-op executives, policy makers and investors to Austin and Miami, the audience a team's other B2B partners want in the suite.

Official Energy Partner designation, livery and race-suit placement, naming of the home-race hospitality, Base Core demonstrations at the US rounds, driver and team content for the Texas and Illinois markets, and an introduction to the Cadillac F1 Team through TWG.

Entry as Official Energy Partner. THREE YEARS, Season 13 to Season 15, covering the national roll-out and a probable listing window. Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 128 · 05 SEP 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 128 · HOT · FE

Antora Energy

Energy Storage · Thermal Batteries for Industry & Data Centres · Sunnyvale, California (factory in San Jose) · Private ($550M Series C, Jul 2026; $2.47B reported)

Antora, the Californian thermal-battery maker whose 5 GWh South Dakota system is one of the largest storage projects in the world, closed an oversubscribed $550M Series C on 30 July 2026, co-led by G2 Venture Partners and Eclipse, to build a second US factory for industry and data centres.

The case

Antora announced on 30 July that it had closed $550M of Series C funding, co-led by G2 Venture Partners and Eclipse, with Ribbit Capital, Salesforce Ventures, StepStone and John Doerr joining Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon and Decarbonization Partners. Total funding stands at $770M; Crunchbase News reports a $2.47B valuation, which the company has not stated. The money funds a second US manufacturing hub and large projects. The proof point landed in May: a 50 MW / 5 GWh thermal battery at POET's Big Stone City plant, built in under twelve months and now delivering energy.

Bloomberg framed the raise around the data-centre boom: Antora stores cheap electricity as heat in solid carbon blocks and returns it around the clock as heat or power, the load-shifting story hyperscalers and utilities are buying. The company says it has signed agreements with hyperscale operators but has not named them. A brand that sells to industrial CFOs, utilities and data-centre developers now needs a national stage on which to say 'reindustrialise America' out loud.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Antora closed an oversubscribed $550M Series C on 30 July 2026, co-led by G2 Venture Partners and Eclipse, with Ribbit Capital, Salesforce Ventures, Activate Capital, John Doerr, Westly Group, StepStone Group and Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures joining existing backers Decarbonization Partners, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, Trust Ventures and Impact Science Ventures. Total funding is $770M. Crunchbase News reports a $2.47B valuation; the company has not stated one, so the brief treats it as reported.
Proof plant, then capital
On 19 May 2026 Antora and POET commissioned a 50 MW / 5 GWh thermal battery at POET's Big Stone City bioprocessing plant in South Dakota, more than 200 batteries, built in under twelve months and one of the largest storage installations in the world. The raise ten weeks later is the scale-up money: a second US manufacturing hub and large projects. A company moving from first plant to national roll-out is at the point where a brand gets built.
The data-centre framing
Bloomberg headlined the round 'amid boom in AI data centers'. Antora says it has signed agreements with hyperscale data-centre operators but has not named them or disclosed capacity. The buyers it needs to reach next are utility executives, industrial CFOs and hyperscaler energy teams, and the message is cheap, round-the-clock power made in America.
Calendar window
Formula E's GEN4 era opens with the Jeddah double-header on 18-19 December 2026. Season 13 then brings a new Austin E-Prix at Circuit of The Americas on 6 February 2027 and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February 2027. A deal agreed this autumn puts Antora on an American car for both US rounds in its first season.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E's roster is TWG AI as primary and AI partner, Quest Global for engineering services, Crowe UK for audit and advisory, Reflo for sustainable sportswear and TWG Motorsports as owner, with Nissan powertrains from Season 13. The sponsor table shows no energy, storage or utility brand on the team: Official Energy Storage Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The American team
Andretti is run from Indianapolis, the only US-owned team on the Formula E grid, and its parent TWG Motorsports also operates the Cadillac Formula 1 team with General Motors. An American energy company whose pitch is reindustrialisation belongs on the American car, and the same owner gives a credible route to F1 if Antora's scale and budget grow.
Two US rounds in one month
Austin on 6 February 2027 is a new venue at Circuit of The Americas and Miami follows on 20 February. Both sit in the states and markets where Antora's industrial and utility customers and the data-centre developers it is courting are based.
A story the team can tell
Formula E's on-track narrative is energy management: how much you store, how efficiently you recover it and when you deploy it. Antora's business is storing cheap electricity and releasing it when it is worth most. That is a content line the team can run all season without inventing a technical link that does not exist.

Value To Andretti Formula E — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Honest MODE B halo
A 50 MW thermal battery is an industrial asset; it will not sit in the garage or power the pit lane. The partnership's value is commercial and it should be sold that way: an American energy brand on an American car in a championship built on electrification.
Commercial lift for the team
Antora brings a guest list the team's other partners want to meet: utility executives, industrial plant owners, hyperscaler energy buyers and state policymakers. Hospitality at Austin and Miami, and a shared industrial-customer programme through TWG Motorsports, turn those guests into pipeline for both sides.
Content and ecosystem
Co-produced explainers on stored heat versus race-day energy recovery, factory-floor content from San Jose and the second US hub, and driver appearances at Antora customer sites and industry events. TWG AI's presence on the same car gives an AI-and-energy pairing that mirrors the data-centre story Antora sells.
What the team gives back
Official Energy Storage Partner designation, sidepod branding, Austin and Miami hospitality, driver and engineering access for Antora's channels, and a documented option to step up to the Cadillac F1 programme under the same ownership.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Energy Storage Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15 (2026/27 to 2028/29), covering the second-factory build and the first hyperscaler projects. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year. Scope: sidepod branding, Austin and Miami hospitality, engineering content, an industrial-customer programme through TWG Motorsports, and an option to step up to the Cadillac F1 team from 2028.

The askA 25-minute call with Andrew Ponec before the Jeddah opener to confirm the round and the second-factory timeline on the record, agree an Austin E-Prix announcement window, and size an Official Energy Storage Partner entry at Andretti Formula E for Seasons 13-15.

Andrew Ponec
Co-Founder & CEO, Antora Energy · verified
Ponec co-founded Antora with Justin Briggs and David Bierman and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Bierman, Co-Founder and Chief Commercial Officer; Briggs, Co-Founder and COO, who owns policy and communications; Rene Griemens, CFO. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the American stage.
“Andrew, you just raised $550M to reindustrialise America. The American Formula E team races in Austin and Miami in February with an open energy lane, and its owner also runs the Cadillac F1 team. 25 minutes to see what the seat costs?”
Bottom line
A $550M round closed on 30 July, one of the largest cleantech raises of the year, a 5 GWh proof plant running in South Dakota, and two US E-Prix in February: Antora has the budget, the story and the stage. Andretti's energy lane is open and its owner offers a path to F1.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential

Intelligence Brief / N° 125 · HOT · FE

Climate Tech - Grid/Energy Management Software - Washington DC · Washington, D.C. · $1.05B valuation (Series A, Aug 2026)

Emerald AI closed a $150M oversubscribed Series A on 25 Aug 2026 at a $1.05B valuation, lifting total funding past $220M. Twelve Fortune Global 500 strategics — including NVIDIA, Siemens and GE Vernova — now hold stakes as the company moves from demonstration to full-scale commercial grid-flex deployment.

The case

Emerald AI raised a $150M oversubscribed Series A on 25 Aug 2026, valuing the grid-flexibility software company at $1.05B and lifting total capital raised past $220M. Energize Capital and DCVC co-led the round, joined by NVIDIA, Siemens, GE Vernova, RWE, Aramco Ventures and Samsung Ventures — twelve Fortune Global 500 companies now hold equity. The raise marks a BRAND RECKONING moment: Emerald moves from demonstration pilots to multi-megawatt, full data-center-scale commercial deployment, and needs a visibility platform to match its new enterprise-trust ambitions.

No F1 or Formula E grid-flexibility sponsor exists on either grid, leaving the energy-management category entirely open. As hyperscalers and utilities scrutinize Emerald's enterprise credentials, a global motorsport platform offers scale-validation no single-utility pilot can match. The slot that matches Emerald's grid-flex narrative architecturally is open at Nissan Formula E Team.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Emerald AI closed a $150M oversubscribed Series A on 25 Aug 2026 at a $1.05B valuation, lifting total funding past $220M, with Energize Capital and DCVC co-leading alongside NVIDIA, Siemens, GE Vernova, RWE, Aramco Ventures and Samsung Ventures.
Budget moment
Fresh capital funds Emerald's shift from demonstration pilots to multi-megawatt, full data-center-scale commercial deployment, creating a first enterprise-marketing budget cycle before the company locks utility and hyperscaler contracts.
Calendar window
The 8-12 week horizon lines up with Formula E's 2026-27 season sponsorship renewal cycle, when grid-partner slots are negotiated before pre-season commitments close.
Competitive clock
No F1 or Formula E grid-flexibility sponsor currently exists on either grid; twelve Fortune Global 500 investors now have incentive to steer their own sponsorship dollars toward the category once Emerald's raise is public.

Proof points — every figure checked against its source (see Sources)

Why Nissan — the open lane, the audience, the platform

Open lane
Nissan Formula E Team carries no grid-flexibility or energy-management partner today, leaving a category lane open on an EV-native grid with no direct precedent among rival teams.
Audience overlap
Formula E's urban, sustainability-literate fanbase and Nissan's global EV customer base overlap directly with the utility and hyperscaler executives Emerald is courting for its next contract cycle.
Activation platform
Nissan's factory operations, simulator facilities and race-weekend garage infrastructure give Emerald live surfaces to demonstrate real-time grid-flex software beyond a logo placement.
Consumption capacity
Nissan's global EV manufacturing scale and existing utility relationships mean the team can credibly co-present Emerald's technology rather than simply carry sponsorship branding.

Value To Nissan Formula E Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream
Emerald Conductor's load-shedding engine could manage Nissan's factory energy draw and simulator compute loads, giving the team a live grid-flex deployment to showcase.
Commercial lift
Sponsorship introduces Emerald to Nissan's existing utility and OEM supplier relationships, widening its pipeline of enterprise pilot customers beyond current strategic investors.
Content and ecosystem
Race-weekend broadcast graphics and factory telemetry walls give Emerald recurring content assets showing real-time grid interaction during ePrix sessions.
What the team gives back
Nissan provides paddock access, factory demonstration space and co-branded content assets in exchange for Emerald's energy-management technology and visibility budget.

Deal architecture

A three-year entry-tier grid-flexibility partnership, in the $2-4M annual range, makes Emerald the team's energy-management partner across the 2026-27 season, with activation anchored at flagship street-circuit race weekends. THREE YEARS secures renewal leverage as Emerald scales from pilot utilities toward full hyperscaler contracts.

The askRequest 25 minutes with Dr. Sivaram's team to scope a three-year entry-tier energy-management partnership ahead of Formula E's 2026-27 sponsorship renewal window.

Primary decision-maker

Dr. Varun Sivaram
Founder & CEO, Emerald AI · verified
Dr. Varun Sivaram founded Emerald AI in 2024 after serving as Chief Technology Officer of ReNew Power, one of India's largest renewable energy companies. He now leads Emerald's push to commercialize grid-flexible AI data-center software with utility and hyperscaler partners nationwide.

Opening angle

Emerald AI just banked $150M at a $1.05B valuation with zero motorsport visibility to match its ambition.
“Emerald just closed a $150M round with NVIDIA and Siemens on the cap table, and Formula E has no grid-flexibility partner on the grid — can we book 25 minutes?”
Bottom line
Emerald AI's $150M Series A, backed by NVIDIA, Siemens and GE Vernova, hands it enterprise credibility but zero motorsport visibility. Nissan Formula E Team is the clean fit: an electrification-native series with no grid-flexibility partner, ready to co-present Emerald's technology to the same utility audiences.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 147 · 12 AUG 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 147 · HOT · F1

Lovable

AI Software Creation · App-Building Platform · Stockholm (US offices opening: San Francisco, New York, Boston) · Private ($13.3B; $400M Series C, Aug 2026)

Lovable, the Stockholm platform on which non-engineers build and run software, announced a $400M Series C at a $13.3B valuation on 12 August, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund, doubling the $6.6B price set in December and funding a US office push.

The case

Lovable confirmed on 12 August a $400M Series C at $13.3B, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, with Balderton, Kaszek, Tencent and Regent joining and Accel, CapitalG, DST and Salesforce Ventures returning. The price has doubled since the $330M Series B at $6.6B on 18 December 2025. The company says revenue run rate passed $500M in June and should reach about $600M by end-August; more than 60 million projects have been built on the platform and its apps draw over 900 million visits a month.

The money is earmarked for scale and for America: Stockholm stays headquarters while offices open in San Francisco, New York and Boston, with about 450 hires planned this year and a chief marketing officer already based in San Francisco. A brand whose customers are founders and business owners in 150 countries now needs a stage those customers watch. It has never bought sport; the first seat is the one that defines the category.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 12 August Lovable announced a $400M Series C at a $13.3B valuation, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, and confirmed the same day by TechCrunch and Bloomberg. The company's own release is the primary source; the run-rate figures in it are company-stated and unaudited.
Price doubled in eight months
The Series B of 18 December 2025 raised $330M at $6.6B; the Series A in July 2025 was $200M at $1.8B. A company re-priced from $1.8B to $13.3B in thirteen months has a story to tell to founders, enterprise buyers and, in time, public-market investors, and a budget to tell it with.
The US build-out
Stockholm remains headquarters, but the round funds offices in San Francisco, New York and Boston and about 450 hires this year. The chief marketing officer is already based in San Francisco. A brand moving its marketing centre of gravity to America needs American reach; F1's US rounds are the most concentrated business audience in sport.
Calendar window
The Dutch and Italian GPs open the run-in after the summer break; the United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the American stages left in 2026. Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and activated in full for 2027.

Why Tgr Haas F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Haas carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner, Haas Automation and Haas Tooling, Mphasis as a digital-services partner, Infobip for fan messaging, CommScope and Ruckus for networking, Alpinestars for kit. Nothing on the roster builds software; Official Software Creation Partner is a clean category and Mphasis, a services integrator, is a channel rather than a rival.
The American team
Haas is the only US-owned team that has raced for a decade, with a Kannapolis base and an owner whose machine-tool business sells to the small manufacturers who are exactly the founders and operators Lovable serves. The Miami, Austin and Las Vegas rounds are its home races, and Lovable's new offices are being opened to reach the same audience.
A team that will use the product
The leanest operation on the grid has the longest list of unbuilt tools. Hospitality, logistics, partner reporting and content sites built by the people who need them, not by race engineers, is the demonstration Lovable sells to every business customer.
Price and access
A mid-grid team offers a first-time sports buyer a full partner designation, on-car placement and hospitality at a fraction of a front-running team's price, with direct access to the team's leadership for a founder-led company.

Value To Tgr Haas F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Internal applications for the commercial and operations staff: guest and hospitality management for the US rounds, freight and travel trackers, partner-activation microsites, driver and content pages, sponsor reporting dashboards. Built on Lovable in days, hosted on the enterprise tier, with the team's data staying inside its own accounts.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner with tens of millions of builders and founders as customers brings a guest list of entrepreneurs, venture investors and enterprise buyers to Austin, Miami and Las Vegas, the audience Haas's B2B partners want in the suite, and a platform for co-marketing with the team's other technology partners.
Content and ecosystem
Build-your-race-app fan activations at the US rounds; founder-and-driver content around what the team built and shipped that week; a reference customer story Lovable's enterprise sales team can tell to every business that runs on tight budgets.
What the team gives back
Official Software Creation Partner designation, sidepod or mirror placement, hospitality at Austin, Miami and Las Vegas, driver and team access for Lovable's channels, and naming of the team's internal-tools programme.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Software Creation Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, covering the US build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in enterprise seats. Scope: sidepod or mirror placement, the team's internal-tools programme, Austin, Miami and Las Vegas hospitality, founder-and-driver content.

The askA 25-minute call with Anton Osika before the United States GP to confirm the marketing owner, agree an Austin or Las Vegas announcement window, and size an Official Software Creation Partner entry against Haas's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Anton Osika
Co-Founder & CEO, Lovable · verified
Osika co-founded Lovable in Stockholm in 2023 and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Fabian Hedin, Co-Founder and CTO, and the San Francisco-based CMO, not named on any leadership page. No CFO or COO is publicly named.

Opening angle

Lead with the American stage.
“Anton, you have just raised $400M to take Lovable to America, and the American team has no software-creation partner. Austin is eleven weeks away. 25 minutes to see what a three-year seat at Haas would cost and return?”
Bottom line
A $400M round at $13.3B, a company-stated run rate near $600M and a US office build-out put Lovable at peak brand-investment authority. Haas is the American team with the software-creation lane open, and two US races sit inside the window.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 153 · 03 AUG 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 153 · HOT · F1

OLIX Computing

AI Semiconductors · Optical Inference Silicon · London (registered St Albans; founded 2024) · Private ($3.3B; $312M Series B, Aug 2026)

OLIX, the London AI-chip company founded in 2024 by James Dacombe, announced a $312M Series B at a $3.3B valuation on 3 August, tripling the $1B mark set by its $220M Series A in February. Arm, Hudson River Trading and Reed Hastings joined; the UK's Sovereign AI fund invested.

The case

Fundomo led the round; Arm, Hudson River Trading and Reed Hastings joined, and existing backers Hummingbird, Plural, Creandum, Crane, Phoenix Court and Transition increased their commitments. Six months earlier Hummingbird had led a $220M Series A at just over $1B. OLIX builds specialised inference silicon connected by an optical network, with first systems due to customers in the second half of 2027. It is recruiting engineers across London, Bristol, Austin, Toronto and San Francisco, has hired former Wise CFO Matt Briers as CFO and put Stanford's Nick McKeown on the board.

The grid has already priced AI silicon: Groq became an Official Partner of McLaren in September 2025 with its inference chips on the car from Singapore, and Arm, now an OLIX investor, sits on Aston Martin Aramco's roster. OLIX is the British entrant without a seat. A company that must recruit against Nvidia and sell to hyperscalers before its first chip ships has a brand to build, and now the money to build it.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
OLIX announced a $312M Series B at a $3.3B valuation on 3 August 2026, led by Fundomo with Arm, Hudson River Trading and Reed Hastings. The company's own newsroom carries the round; Tech.eu, DCD and The Next Web report the same figures.
Tripled in six months
The $220M Series A in February 2026, led by Hummingbird, priced OLIX at just over $1B. Six months later the Series B priced it at $3.3B. A company re-rated that fast, before its first chip ships, is being valued on narrative, and narrative is what a sponsorship builds.
The 2027 launch
First AI systems are due to customers in the second half of 2027. A three-season partnership starting in 2027 puts the brand on the grid in the launch year, with an evaluation clause that turns the halo into a reference deployment once product exists.
Calendar window
Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP in Austin, where OLIX is recruiting, falls in late October; Las Vegas follows in November. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced there and activated in full for 2027.

Williams is rebuilding a technical base against far larger incumbents; OLIX is doing the same against Nvidia. That parallel gives the partnership a narrative the team can tell on camera without stretching.
Talent and the United States
OLIX is hiring in London, Bristol, Austin, Toronto and San Francisco. An F1 engineering brand is a recruitment asset in every one of those markets, and the Austin office gives the United States GP a home-market activation.

$312M at $3.3B, a government-backed sovereign-AI story and an open silicon lane at a British team make OLIX a 2027 partner to sign in the fourth quarter. The pre-product timeline and the absence of a marketing owner hold the score at 70.

Horizon3, the San Francisco security company whose NodeZero platform attacks customers' networks the way an adversary would, announced a $250M Series E at a valuation above $2B on 3 August, co-led by NightDragon and NEA, tripling the $650M price of its June 2025 Series D in little over a year.

The case

The oversubscribed round brought in Acrew, Blue Cloud Ventures, Demeter, Singapore's EDBI, PSG, SAIC and Sapphire, with Craft, Prosperity7, Qualcomm Ventures, Ridge and SignalFire returning. The company reports 120% year-on-year ARR growth and more than 7,000 organisations protected, four of them Fortune 10; TechCrunch puts ARR near $100M (reported). Founders Snehal Antani and Anthony Pillitiere met at Joint Special Operations Command; Antani was later CTO of Splunk. The money funds international expansion, with offices opened in Amsterdam in June, Australia and Singapore, and a partner network.

Cybersecurity is the most-sold technology category on the grid: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, Okta and Rubrik at McLaren, Cato Networks at Alpine, and Red Bull's 1Password. Every one sells defence. Horizon3 sells the attack, continuously, and its new CMO Andres Botero ran marketing at Rubrik in the period its McLaren partnership was being built. A $2B category leader with no seat, and a marketer who has watched one taken.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Horizon3 announced a $250M Series E at a valuation above $2B on 3 August 2026, co-led by NightDragon and NEA, with seven new investors including Sapphire Ventures, PSG, SAIC and Singapore's EDBI. The company release and TechCrunch carry the same figures.
Tripled in a year
The June 2025 Series D, $100M led by NEA, valued the company at $650M (reported). Fourteen months later the price is above $2B, on 120% year-on-year ARR growth and more than 7,000 organisations protected, four of them Fortune 10. A brand re-rated that fast has a story to tell and the budget to tell it.
A marketing owner with a mandate
Andres Botero joined as Chief Marketing Officer on 7 January 2026 from Rubrik, where he was CMO through the April 2024 IPO. Rubrik's multi-year McLaren partnership was announced three weeks after his move; whether he built it is not confirmed, but he has seen the mechanics from the inside.
Calendar window
The United States GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026, with Mexico City and São Paulo between them; teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced there and activated in full for 2027.

Why Cadillac F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Cadillac's debut roster carries TWG AI as exclusive AI partner, Core Scientific for the data centre, IFS for enterprise software, plus Claro, Jim Beam, Tenneco and Tommy Hilfiger. No cybersecurity partner: Official Cybersecurity Partner is a clean category on a team that has said it wants fewer, bigger partners.
A greenfield estate
New factories in Fishers, Charlotte and Silverstone, a supplier base assembled in two years and a garage network rebuilt at every circuit. F1 teams have faced phishing, deepfake and telemetry-theft campaigns and a 2025 FIA systems loophole. A first-season estate is the one most in need of continuous attack testing.
An American story
Horizon3's founders met at Joint Special Operations Command and SAIC has joined the register. Cadillac is the GM-backed American flag-bearer with a commercial team hired from the Miami GP and Unilever to sell exactly that audience.
The buyer in the suite
Cadillac's hospitality reaches CISOs, CIOs and federal buyers at Austin and Las Vegas, the audience a $100M-ARR security company selling to Fortune 10 accounts wants in the room.

Value To Cadillac F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
NodeZero runs autonomous penetration tests continuously across the team's factory networks, trackside infrastructure, supplier integrations and partner environments, ranking findings by exploitability and re-testing after each fix. The team's security staff work from a live attacker's view rather than an annual audit.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner that sells to Fortune 10 CISOs and defence agencies brings a guest list of security and federal buyers to the US rounds, the audience Cadillac's B2B partners want alongside them.
Content and ecosystem
How a brand-new Formula 1 team defends itself: co-produced engineering content on continuous security validation, a reference customer for Horizon3's enterprise sales, and a story that fits a debutant building everything from scratch.
What the team gives back
Official Cybersecurity Partner designation, car and garage placement, naming of the security-validation programme, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, driver and engineering access for Horizon3's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Cybersecurity Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the international build-out. Estimated $4-6M a year, part-payable in NodeZero licences. Scope: car and garage placement, naming of the team's security-validation programme, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for CISOs and federal buyers, content on how a new team defends itself.

The askA 25-minute call with Andres Botero before the United States GP to test appetite for a 2027 start, clear the AI-partner language with Cadillac's TWG AI exclusivity, and size an Official Cybersecurity Partner entry, part-paid in NodeZero licences, against the team's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Andres Botero
Chief Marketing Officer, Horizon3.ai · verified
Botero joined on 7 January 2026 from Rubrik, where he was CMO through its April 2024 IPO and while the McLaren partnership announced on 28 January was built; his part in that deal is not confirmed. Sponsor: Snehal Antani, co-founder and CEO. Path: Holly Grey, CFO, and Matt Hartley, CRO.

Opening angle

Lead with Rubrik and the empty lane.
“Andres, you were at Rubrik while its McLaren deal came together. Cadillac has no cybersecurity partner and a first-season estate nobody has attacked yet. 25 minutes before Austin to see what NodeZero on a Formula 1 team looks like?”
Bottom line
$250M at more than $2B, 120% ARR growth, a CMO who has seen an F1 deal built and an open cybersecurity lane at the American debutant put Horizon3 at peak authority to move, with Austin and Las Vegas inside the window. The TWG AI exclusivity and a premium first-deal price hold the score at 78.

The case

ThreatLocker announced a $190M Series F on 29 July 2026, led by Elephant, with D. E. Shaw Ventures and Arthur Ventures returning and Koch Disruptive Technologies new. It follows a $20M Series B, $100M Series C, $115M Series D (April 2024) and $60M Series E (April 2025): nearly $500M in total. SecurityWeek puts the pre-round valuation at $1.6B (reported); the company has not stated a new one and publishes no revenue. The platform, allowlisting and Ringfencing that block whatever is not explicitly permitted, protects more than 70,000 organisations. The round funds AI-risk controls and a Reading office.

Cybersecurity is the most-sold technology category on the grid: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, 1Password (Red Bull) and Cato Networks at Alpine. Each vendor bought the same thing, a paddock full of the enterprise buyers it sells to. ThreatLocker reaches the mid-market through managed service providers and has just committed to Europe. What it lacks is a brand stage for those partners and their customers.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
ThreatLocker announced on 29 July 2026 that it had secured $190M in Series F funding led by Elephant, with D. E. Shaw Ventures and Arthur Ventures continuing and Koch Disruptive Technologies investing for the first time. The company's own release names the uses: controls for AI-related security risks, the Zero Trust Platform, and international expansion starting with a Reading, UK office.
Six rounds, near $500M
The Series F follows a $20M Series B, $100M Series C, $115M Series D in April 2024 and $60M Series E in April 2025, taking total funding to nearly $500M. SecurityWeek reports the previous round valued the company at $1.6B; ThreatLocker has not stated a Series F valuation and does not publish revenue, so the brief sizes capacity on the raise, not the valuation.
Europe is the next spend
The company already runs its European headquarters from Dublin, with offices in Dubai and Brisbane. Reading is the first UK office, which puts a brand-building budget in the same country as eight Formula 1 teams and Silverstone, where Cadillac's UK operation sits.
Update since this date: a first motorsport trial
On 4 September 2026 ThreatLocker joined Juncos Hollinger Racing for the IndyCar season finale at Laguna Seca, a one-race presence on the JHR entry. Danny Jenkins said the aim was to introduce ThreatLocker to the IndyCar community. The company has now tested motorsport with a single-race buy; the next conversation is whether a multi-year F1 seat at an Indiana-based team is the scale-up.

Cadillac is building an entire Formula 1 operation from scratch: a $200M, roughly 400,000 sq ft campus in Fishers next to Indianapolis Metropolitan Airport, a Charlotte facility and a Silverstone base. Core Scientific is developing the team's Indianapolis data hub and optimising the cloud-hybrid environment across US and UK operations; IFS runs operations. There is no cybersecurity partner on the roster, which the team's profile lists as an open category.
Fewer, bigger partners
Cadillac has said it is not seeking a title sponsor for its debut and wants fewer, bigger partnerships. That favours a partner whose product is deployed across the team rather than a badge, which is the shape of a zero-trust endpoint deal.
Home market
ThreatLocker is headquartered in Orlando and sells mainly through US managed service providers. Cadillac is the American entry, with the Miami, Austin and Las Vegas rounds each year, and its Indiana base sits in the same city as the IndyCar team ThreatLocker has just tried.
Ruled out by the table
Every established security lane is taken: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, 1Password (Red Bull), Cato Networks at Alpine and NinjaOne at Audi. Of the open teams, Cadillac's combination of a new estate, a US identity and an explicit open category is the strongest.

Value To Cadillac F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
A debut team is defining its security baseline now. ThreatLocker's allowlisting denies any application not explicitly permitted, Ringfencing restricts how permitted applications touch data and each other, and Elevation Control removes standing admin rights: controls that fit engineering workstations, machining and additive cells, the Indianapolis data hub and trackside laptops that join a different circuit network every race weekend.
Cost-cap arithmetic
A default-deny posture stops ransomware and rogue tooling without the headcount of a large security operations centre, which matters for a team spending inside the FIA cost cap. Product and services can form part of the consideration, lowering the cash element.
Commercial lift for the team
ThreatLocker's channel is thousands of managed service providers and 70,000 end customers, a mid-market audience Cadillac's B2B partners do not yet reach. US-race hospitality for MSP partners and a factory reference story give the team a new pool of guests and prospects.
What the team gives back
Official Zero Trust Cybersecurity Partner designation, halo or sidepod placement, a published deployment case study with the team's IT leadership, hospitality at the US rounds, and driver and engineering access for ThreatLocker's channel events.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Zero Trust Cybersecurity Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, covering the Reading launch and any listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in product and services. Scope: halo or sidepod placement, deployment across the team's estate, US-race hospitality for MSP partners, factory content.

The askA 25-minute call with Danny Jenkins before the United States GP to confirm the Series F valuation on the record, walk through Cadillac's estate build-out, and size an Official Zero Trust Cybersecurity Partner entry against the team's 2027 roster.

Danny Jenkins
CEO & Co-Founder, ThreatLocker · verified
Jenkins co-founded ThreatLocker in Orlando in 2017 after building Dublin email-security vendor MXSweep, and fronts every raise and sponsorship. Path: Sami Jenkins, COO and Co-Founder; Shane Deegan, Chief Revenue Officer. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Lead with the greenfield estate.
“Danny, Cadillac is building its security stack from zero in Indiana and Silverstone, and there is no cybersecurity partner on the car. Your Series F just paid for Europe; an American team gives your 70,000 customers and MSPs the story. 25 minutes before Austin?”
Bottom line
A $190M Series F closed on 29 July, a first European office and a platform protecting 70,000 organisations put ThreatLocker at peak spend authority. Cadillac's roster has no cybersecurity partner, the team is building its estate now, and two US races remain inside the window.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 165 · 08 JUL 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 165 · HOT · F1

Keyfactor

Cybersecurity · Machine Identity / PKI / Post-Quantum · Independence, Ohio · Private ($1B+ round, Jul 2026; valuation undisclosed)

Keyfactor, the Ohio machine-identity and PKI company, announced a $1B+ strategic growth investment led by Summit Partners on 6 July 2026, with Insight Partners and Sixth Street Growth staying in. Private-equity money with a mandate for scale, arriving as post-quantum migration turns its category into a board topic.

The case

On 6 July Keyfactor announced a $1B+ strategic growth investment led by Summit Partners; Insight Partners and Sixth Street Growth keep significant stakes and the valuation was not disclosed. It follows $77M from Insight in 2019, $125M with the PrimeKey merger in 2021 and a Sixth Street minority round at about $1.3B in October 2023. The company manages billions of machine identities a year for more than 2,500 customers in 150 countries, over 40% of the Fortune 100 among them, and reached FedRAMP status this year. Stated use of funds: product, expansion, team, acquisitions.

Cybersecurity is a proven Formula 1 category: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Keeper at Williams, 1Password at Red Bull, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Okta at McLaren and, since November 2025, SEALSQ's post-quantum chips at Alpine. Machine identity, the layer beneath all of them, is not yet on the grid. Keyfactor's automotive practice already issues certificate identities to vehicles and signs their firmware, which is the language a works team owned by a carmaker speaks.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 6 July 2026 Keyfactor announced a $1B+ strategic growth investment led by Summit Partners. Insight Partners and Sixth Street Growth keep significant ownership after the close. The valuation was not disclosed, and the brief does not guess one.
A scale mandate
The stated use of funds is product innovation, geographic expansion, team building and strategic acquisitions. Growth equity of this size is deployed against a plan to become the category name, and a category name needs reach outside the security conference circuit: the boardrooms of banks, retailers and government buyers.
The post-quantum clock
Keyfactor's own framing of the round is securing the AI and post-quantum enterprise. Migration to quantum-safe cryptography is now a dated programme in the regulated industries it sells to, which makes trust infrastructure a board-level topic rather than an IT line item for the first time.
Calendar window
Cadillac's debut season still has the US GP in Austin in October and the Las Vegas GP in November, and teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and activated in full for 2027.

Proof points — every figure checked against its source (see Sources)

Why Cadillac F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Cadillac's inaugural roster is TWG AI, Core Scientific, IFS, Claro, Tenneco, Tommy Hilfiger, Jim Beam, Pirelli and Alpinestars, with General Motors as parent. There is no cybersecurity or identity partner, and the team's own profile lists cybersecurity as an open category. Six other teams have already proved the category sells.
A carmaker parent
General Motors is the works owner. Vehicle and ECU identity, secure over-the-air updates and firmware signing are Keyfactor's automotive practice, so the conversation with the team's parent starts in a language both sides already speak.
A team that will use the product
A debut team is building its factory, trackside and car-software estate from scratch. Certificate automation and code signing installed in year one become the team's standard, which is the difference between a technology partner and a logo.
An American story
An Ohio company on the American team, activated at Austin and Las Vegas, where Keyfactor's banking, retail and federal buyers can be hosted, and where the team's debut-season attention is highest.

Value To Cadillac F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Automated certificate lifecycle across the team's servers, telemetry links, simulators and supplier connections; code signing for the software deployed to the car and the pit wall; a post-quantum readiness plan for the estate. The team gets a security baseline it would otherwise have to buy and staff.
Commercial lift for the team
Keyfactor sells to chief information security officers and chief information officers at banks, retailers, telecoms and federal agencies. That guest list at Austin and Las Vegas is the audience Cadillac's other technology partners want in the suite.
Content and ecosystem
Co-produced engineering content on securing a race team, a reference deployment for Keyfactor's enterprise sales, and a story that runs from the car's software to the parent's connected vehicles.
What the team gives back
Official Cybersecurity Partner designation, rear-wing endplate or halo placement, naming of the team's trust infrastructure, hospitality at the two US rounds, driver and engineering access for Keyfactor's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Cybersecurity Partner (machine identity). THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, matching the post-quantum migration window and a probable exit path for Summit. Estimated $3-5M a year, part in platform services. Scope: endplate or halo placement, naming of the team's trust infrastructure, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, technical content.

The askA 25-minute call with Jordan Rackie before the US GP to agree an Austin announcement window and size an Official Cybersecurity Partner entry against Cadillac's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Jordan Rackie
Chief Executive Officer, Keyfactor · verified
Rackie has led Keyfactor since May 2019, through the PrimeKey merger and three institutional rounds; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Mike Volanoski, President and Chief Revenue Officer (sales, marketing, channel; since January 2026); Jamie Walker, Chief Marketing Officer; Scott Meyerhoff, CFO.

Opening angle

Lead with the category precedent.
“Jordan, six Formula 1 teams already carry a security partner and none carries the machine-identity layer beneath them. Cadillac is the American debut and the lane is open. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A $1B+ round led by Summit Partners, a category the grid has validated six times over, and a debut American team that lists cybersecurity as an open lane put Keyfactor at peak brand-investment authority with a clean seat available. Two US races remain inside the window.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 170 · 01 JUL 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 170 · HOT · F1

Together AI

AI Infrastructure · Open-Source AI Cloud / Inference · San Francisco (founded 2022) · Private ($8.3B post-money; $800M Series C, Jul 2026)

Together AI, the San Francisco cloud built for open-source AI, closed an $800M Series C at an $8.3B valuation on 1 July 2026, led by Aramco Ventures with Nvidia, Vista and General Catalyst: two and a half times its February 2025 price, with annual bookings past $1.15B.
