The case

Together AI announced on 1 July 2026 an $800M Series C at an $8.3B post-money valuation, led by Aramco Ventures with Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, Nvidia, March Capital, Pegatron and S Ventures. Annual bookings topped $1.15B in the last quarter, with thousands of paying customers including Cursor, Cognition and Decagon. The $305M Series B at $3.3B, led by General Catalyst, closed only in February 2025. The company says its infrastructure footprint will grow roughly 50-fold over five years: for an infrastructure business, the brand-building moment arrives with the build-out.

The grid has already priced the neocloud archetype: CoreWeave became Aston Martin Aramco's Official AI Cloud Computing Partner in May 2025, Core Scientific and TWG AI opened on Cadillac's first roster, and Groq holds inference silicon on McLaren's. Aramco, the lead investor here, is both F1's Global Partner and the Aston Martin title, so the ecosystem knows the name; the seat, though, has to be one CoreWeave does not already hold.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 1 July 2026 Together AI announced an $800M Series C at an $8.3B post-money valuation, led by Aramco Ventures with Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, Nvidia, March Capital, Pegatron and S Ventures. This is a company release, not a press report, so the figures are confirmed.
Price up two and a half times in sixteen months
The $305M Series B at $3.3B, led by General Catalyst, closed in February 2025. Annual bookings passed $1.15B in the quarter before the Series C, with thousands of paying customers including Cursor, Cognition and Decagon. A company re-priced that fast, selling to developers and enterprises, has a story to tell and a budget to tell it with.
A build-out that needs a name
Management says the infrastructure footprint will grow roughly 50-fold over five years. An infrastructure brand is built while the capacity is built: the enterprise buyers, bankers and hyperscaler partners it must win are exactly the audience an F1 paddock assembles.
Calendar window
Brand budgets are set in the quarter after a raise and teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US stages on which a San Francisco company would announce. Since this brief's date, IBM signed a $240M multi-year agreement (11 August 2026) to host a Together AI inference cluster on IBM Cloud from the first quarter of 2027, which strengthens the capacity story rather than changing the recommendation.

Why Tgr Haas F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
The Haas technology roster is Toyota Gazoo Racing (title), Mphasis (IT services), CommScope and Ruckus (networking) and Infobip (cloud communications), joined in July 2026 by Exein for device-level security. There is no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner: Official AI Cloud Partner is a clean category, and Haas partnerships are priced below the front of the grid.
The American team
Haas is run from Kannapolis, North Carolina, and is the only US-owned team on the grid until Cadillac's arrival this season. A San Francisco company gets a home team for Miami, Austin and Las Vegas and a story that plays to the US enterprise market where its customers sit.
A team that will use the product
A team without a hyperscaler partner buys its compute at list price. Elastic GPU clusters for surrogate models, simulation and analytics, and private inference for engineering assistants, are consumed in the factory rather than displayed on the car, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.
The ecosystem path
Aramco, the round's lead investor, is F1's Global Partner and the title partner at Aston Martin through 2028, so the sport already knows the name. That path leads into F1, not to a specific team: at Aston Martin the lane belongs to CoreWeave, which is why the recommendation is Haas.

Value To Tgr Haas F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Together Instant GPU Clusters are self-service and spin up in minutes; the Frontier AI Factory offers dedicated Blackwell clusters at scale. For Haas that means on-demand capacity for machine-learning surrogates, strategy and driver-in-the-loop simulation, and telemetry and video analytics between sessions, without capital tied up inside the cost cap.
Private inference for the engineering office
Open models fine-tuned on the team's own documentation and data, served from private endpoints, give engineers and strategists assistants that never send team data to a third-party model. That is the concrete product a team without a hyperscaler partner cannot buy cheaply elsewhere.
Commercial lift for the team
Together sells to developers, CTOs and hyperscalers. Its guest list at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas is enterprise buyers, investors and bankers: the audience Haas's B2B partners (Mphasis, CommScope, Infobip) want in the suite.
What the team gives back
Official AI Cloud Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at the three US rounds, and co-produced engineering content from Kannapolis for Together's developer channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Cloud Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the 50-fold build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in compute credits. Scope: sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the team's compute environment, US-round hospitality, engineering content.

The askA 25-minute call with Vipul Ved Prakash before the United States GP to test appetite for a first sports partnership, agree an Austin or Las Vegas announcement window, and size an Official AI Cloud Partner entry against the Haas 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Vipul Ved Prakash
Co-Founder & CEO, Together AI · verified
Prakash co-founded Together AI in 2022 after selling Topsy to Apple and leading search and AI for Siri; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Kai Mak, Chief Revenue Officer, Charles Zedlewski, Chief Product Officer, Meicheng Shi, SVP Finance. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the Aramco connection.
“Vipul, your lead investor is F1's Global Partner, and CoreWeave took its Aston Martin seat the year it listed. The American team has no compute partner. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
An $800M round at $8.3B, bookings above $1.15B and a 50-fold build-out put Together AI at peak brand-investment authority with an F1-literate lead investor. The compute lane at TGR Haas is open and the US rounds sit inside the planning window.

review.reason: contradicted: The event is real and inside the window, but the signal as recorded does not survive the primary source. The thin row read it as a $1.75B venture-style 'strategic financing' of an 'AI-compute energy infrastructure' company suited to Formula E. The company release (Business Wire, 1 Jul 2026) and National Grid's own release (PR Newswire, 1 Jul 2026) say National Grid Ventures agreed to invest $1.75B for a 35% equity stake in Joulent LLC, a Houston developer of natural-gas power plants that launched from stealth on 22 Jun 2026 after three years of incubation inside Engine No. 1. Its flagship, Project Kilby, is a ~2.67 GW gas-fired facility in West Texas, a 50/50 venture with Chevron, supplying a Microsoft-operated data-centre campus under a 20-year PPA with GE Vernova turbines and first power targeted for 2028. So: (1) the capital is a utility buying into project equity, not a growth round that funds brand-building; (2) the business is gas-fired baseload generation for one hyperscaler customer, which contradicts the Formula E sustainability positioning the row assumed and leaves no consumer or broad-B2B audience a sponsorship would reach; (3) the leadership found (Chris James, Founder & CEO, also founder of Engine No. 1; Brian Boland, EVP, CFO & Head of Strategy; Chris Wissel-Tyson, SVP Growth & Strategy; Noah Tulsky, VP Corporate Development) shows no marketing or brand function, and no motorsport tie was found for any of them. Re-open only if Joulent itself announces a corporate brand programme or an F1-relevant energy technology (e.g. trackside power) rather than plant development.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 183 · 22 JUN 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 183 · HOT · FE

Lime

Shared Electric Micromobility · E-bikes and E-scooters · San Francisco (about 230 cities, 29 countries) · Nasdaq: LIME (roadshow live; pricing expected next week)

Lime launched its IPO roadshow on 22 June: 6.96M shares at $24-$26, up to about $181M at a valuation of up to about $1.8B (Renaissance Capital), Nasdaq ticker LIME. A profitable, electric, city-centre mobility brand is about to become public in the cities where Formula E races.

The case

Lime announced the roadshow on 22 June with pricing expected the following week; Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan lead the books and Uber, holder of 24.4% pre-IPO, has indicated interest in up to $20M of shares. The business on sale is no longer a scooter story: FY2025 revenue was $886.7M, up 29%, with adjusted EBITDA of $218.1M and free cash flow of $103.8M, a third positive year, against a $59.3M net loss driven by debt costs. Proceeds repay a $115M term loan at 10% due in September 2026, which frees the cash flow behind it.

A newly listed consumer brand needs a public-market story about scale and cities, and Formula E races in Lime's cities. London, where Lime has served more than 400,000 customers, hosts the season finale on 15-16 August; Berlin and Madrid follow in the GEN4 season. No shared-mobility brand has ever raced on the grid, so the first one defines the category.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 22 June 2026 Lime announced the launch of its IPO roadshow: 6,956,522 shares (6,679,791 from Lime, 276,731 from selling stockholders) at $24-$26, listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as LIME, with Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan leading. Renaissance Capital sized the deal at up to $181M and a valuation of up to $1.8B; pricing was expected the following week.
The business behind the listing
FY2025 revenue was $886.7M, up 29%, adjusted EBITDA $218.1M, operating income $70.4M and free cash flow $103.8M, the third positive year. The $59.3M net loss is a debt-cost story: proceeds repay a $115M term loan at 10% due September 2026. After the listing Lime's cash flow is its own.
A public brand needs a public story
Uber, Lime's largest holder at 24.4%, has indicated interest in up to $20M of shares. A newly public consumer brand has to explain to investors and city governments why it belongs in the centre of cities. Formula E's street circuits in London, Berlin, Madrid, Miami and Austin are that argument on television.
Update since issue
The IPO priced on 30 June 2026 at $25, the mid-point, and trading began on 1 July; TechCrunch reported $167M raised at an implied valuation of about $1.66B (about $174M including selling stockholders). The London E-Prix on 15-16 August remains the first activation window; Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18-19 December.

Why Envision Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Envision Racing's roster is Envision Group (title), Sand Technologies, Teijin and Genpact. No Formula E team carries a shared-mobility, e-bike or e-scooter partner, so Official Micromobility Partner is a first-of-category designation at a team-partner price.
Climate identity
Envision Racing built its brand on the Race Against Climate Change programme; Lime's pitch to cities is car-trip replacement. The two stories are the same story, told to fans and to city halls.
Independent, not a works team
Six Formula E teams are owned by car makers or two-wheel makers (Jaguar, Nissan, Porsche, Cupra, Citroën, Mahindra, and Yamaha in the Lola entry). An independent team can put a scooter brand on the car without an OEM marketing department objecting.
London is home for both
Envision is British-based and the London E-Prix is its home race. Lime has served more than 400,000 London customers and runs both e-bikes and e-scooters there. A finale activation in August needs only a July decision.

Value To Envision Racing — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Race-week mechanics (Mode B)
Lime rider zones and ticket-holder ride credits at the London, Berlin and Madrid E-Prix; Envision-liveried e-bikes in each host city during race week; push and in-app messaging to riders in those cities. The team gets a city-wide presence for a city race.
Audience the roster lacks
Envision's partners are industrial and enterprise brands. Lime brings a consumer audience across about 230 cities and the Uber ecosystem behind its largest shareholder, which is reach the team cannot buy at this price elsewhere.
Content
Driver and team commutes on Lime, a season-long 'last mile to the grid' series, and a shared climate-impact scoreboard built from Lime's ride data and the team's Race Against Climate Change reporting.
What Envision gives back
Official Micromobility Partner designation, car and race-suit placement, host-city activation rights, hospitality at London and Berlin, and a public-company partner announcement timed to the GEN4 launch in December.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Micromobility Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, the whole first GEN4 cycle. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year plus in-kind fleet and ride credits. Scope: car and suit placement, host-city activation in Lime cities, app and rider communications, hospitality at London and Berlin.

The askA 25-minute call with Wayne Ting in the week after pricing to agree a London E-Prix activation for 15-16 August and size a three-season Official Micromobility Partner entry with Envision Racing for the GEN4 era.

Primary decision-maker

Wayne Ting
Chief Executive Officer, Lime · verified
Ting has run Lime since May 2020, joining in 2018 after four years at Uber including Chief of Staff to its CEO. Path: Joseph Kraus, President; Ann Gugino, CFO since December 2023; Hannah McClellan Richards, COO from June 2026. No chief marketing officer is listed among the executive officers.

Opening angle

Lead with the cities.
“Wayne, you are about to list a brand that lives in London, Berlin and Madrid, and Formula E races in all three. No mobility brand has ever been on that grid. 25 minutes after pricing to see how Envision would put Lime in the finale?”
Bottom line
A profitable electric mobility brand listing on Nasdaq this month, an open micromobility lane on every Formula E roster, and a season finale in its biggest European market eight weeks out. Envision Racing is the clean, independent, climate-led home; the deal is small, in-kind heavy and time-bound.

Risks & counters

A SCOOTER BRAND IN A B2B PADDOCK
Lime is a consumer brand with thin margins after debt; a sponsorship line competes with city-licence costs and fleet capex. Counter: Size the entry at the low end and weight it to in-kind fleet and ride credits, which cost Lime little.
LISTING FIRST, BRAND SECOND
Pricing and the quiet period come before any marketing decision; the window may not open until the first public quarter. Counter: Approach after pricing with a London-finale package that needs only a July decision.
